questions.question: Why does MoRo not need floor tape or magnetic strips to find its way?
options: It builds a LiDAR map and locates itself against it using SLAM
It follows a wire buried beneath the factory floor along each route
An operator steers it remotely through every move from a control desk
questions.feedback: Correct. LiDAR plus SLAM replaces the fixed infrastructure that older AGV systems relied on.

questions.question: Which MoRo variant has a 500 kg payload rating, typically used for machine tending and part transfer?
questions.feedback: Correct. The A-500 carries 500 kg and is typically used for machine tending and part transfer.

questions.question: Which of these is a limit of what MoRo can do?
options: Handle a genuinely unplanned situation without human input
Avoid an obstacle that appears in its path, using its sensors
Return to charge itself when needed
questions.feedback: Correct. MoRo follows programmed logic; unplanned situations still need human judgment.

questions.question: How does MoRo change the nature of a floor operator's work?
options: Operators are no longer needed on the floor
Work shifts from performing manual transport toward supervising it
Operators must steer each individual move manually
questions.feedback: Correct. The operator's role moves toward supervision, watching for exceptions and confirming handoffs.

questions.question: What does a LiDAR sensor measure to work out distance?
options: The temperature of nearby objects, read through the sensor window
The sound of nearby machinery, picked up by the sensor head
The time laser light takes to reflect back
questions.feedback: Correct. LiDAR calculates distance from the return time of reflected laser light.

questions.question: Which of these is LiDAR least reliable at detecting?
options: A concrete pillar
A glass panel
A steel machine housing
questions.feedback: Correct. Transparent materials like glass do not reflect the laser predictably.

questions.question: A factory relocates several machines to new positions. What should happen to MoRo's map?
options: Nothing, because the map is permanent once built
MoRo should keep using the old map and ignore the change
It should be updated to reflect the new layout
questions.feedback: Correct. Maps are not permanent and need updating when the layout changes.

questions.question: Which MoRo variant is rated for ±20mm positioning accuracy?
options: The A-250, the lightest of the three variants
The A-1200
The A-500, the mid-range variant
questions.feedback: Correct. The A-250 and A-500 are rated at ±10mm; the A-1200 is rated at ±20mm.

questions.question: What is the name of MoRo's Human-Machine Interface?
options: SLAM
ANT
LiDAR
questions.feedback: Correct. ANT is the HMI used for fleet monitoring and mission control.

questions.question: After power-on, what should an operator wait for before assigning a mission?
options: Approval from the maintenance team that the unit has been serviced this week
A ready state, confirmed after MoRo's internal diagnostic completes
A message from the DiFacto office
questions.feedback: Correct. Assigning work before diagnostics complete is a common, avoidable cause of interrupted starts.

questions.question: While MoRo is under manual override, what is the status of its safety systems?
options: They stay active; override does not disable them
They are switched off until the override has ended
Only the interactive zone is disabled during override
questions.feedback: Correct. Manual override never bypasses safety systems.

questions.question: What is the difference between pausing a mission and cancelling it?
options: Pausing holds position and resumes from the same point; cancelling does not
There is no difference between them
Pausing sends MoRo straight back to its charger
questions.feedback: Correct. A paused mission keeps its state and resumes where it stopped.

questions.question: Which two safety standards is MoRo's safety engineered against, at this level?
options: ISO 9001 and ANSI Z10, the quality and safety management standards
IEC 61131 and ISO 14001
ISO 3691-4 and ANSI B56.5
questions.feedback: Correct. ISO 3691-4 covers industrial trucks; ANSI B56.5 covers guided industrial vehicles.

questions.question: What is MoRo's current interactive zone distance, per DiFacto's guidance?
options: 5 meters
2 meters
10 meters
questions.feedback: Correct. The interactive zone is currently 2 meters, and may be revised as the specification is finalized.

questions.question: When is E-stop the right tool to use?
options: A genuine safety concern needing immediate action
To pause a mission for a short break during a shift
At the end of every shift, to shut the unit down safely
questions.feedback: Correct. E-stop is reserved for genuine safety concerns, not routine pausing.

questions.question: MoRo is stationary in an aisle. What is the safest assumption?
options: It has finished and will stay put
It has failed, so it is safe to push by hand
It may only be paused and could move again
questions.feedback: Correct. A stationary MoRo may simply be paused, so situational awareness still applies.

questions.question: Why might MoRo slow down when someone hesitates near its path?
options: It is signalling a malfunction
It is waiting for the person to give it a clear hand signal first
Its sensors read the unpredictable movement and respond to it
questions.feedback: Correct. MoRo responds to what its sensors detect, not to what a person intends.

questions.question: A situation arises that calls for a judgment call or an exception. Who is responsible for making it?
options: MoRo, because it is autonomous
The nearest MoRo unit in the fleet, through the fleet system
A human, because MoRo only executes programmed logic
questions.feedback: Correct. Judgment calls remain a human responsibility.

questions.question: You notice something minor but unusual about MoRo's path. What is the expected response?
options: Raise it early with your supervisor or designated contact
Wait to see whether it happens again
Diagnose and fix it yourself first
questions.feedback: Correct. Early escalation, even of minor observations, is standard practice.

questions.question: Which habit is appropriate around an active MoRo?
options: Give it room to complete its path
Squeeze past it in tight spaces to save time
Rest a small item on it briefly
questions.feedback: Correct. Treat MoRo with the same predictable attention as any moving industrial equipment.
